Identification and verdict
@botiverse/porthole 0.9.0 (npm), SHA256
 d8014fd0233a6f94354ccb501d99077448eb39ab3d5ac88031bdc3ade52c1033
BENIGN: host-side sandbox and its explicitly registered conformance tests.
The evidence is the local response/data flow and release changes, independent
of scanner severity and registry reputation. Deployment context is unavailable;
this judgment concerns the published package's observed behavior.

Release comparison
Fetched official npm tarballs for 0.8.0 (immediate predecessor) and 0.7.0:
 https://registry.npmjs.org/@botiverse/porthole/-/porthole-0.8.0.tgz
 https://registry.npmjs.org/@botiverse/porthole/-/porthole-0.7.0.tgz
All three archives match their registry SHA512 integrity values.
0.8.0 SHA256 a2cfe3eba418d229e5180d95dae1becd320dcb0eb97b72138d4988062e05d348
0.7.0 SHA256 c97da9418d39d88cf7ea6be480cbb35a3267bdf02eb38229a960f2436d379c95

The cookie module is absent in 0.7.0. Its served.url.framed test instead marks
WebKit as an expected failure based on browserName. In 0.8.0 and 0.9.0 the
cookies.ts and emitted cookies.js are byte-identical: the test measures cookie
retention using keepsFramedCookies, rather than assuming the engine's policy.
The immediate predecessor therefore also fires the old cookie URL matcher;
0.7.0 is the earlier version preceding that addition. Its scan was inspected.

0.8.0 -> 0.9.0 changes seven source files, all concerning annotations:
 annotate/types.ts, annotate/validate.ts, host/create-host.ts,
 platform/types.ts, platform/web.ts, react/frame.tsx, shell/annotate.ts.
Adds count bubbles, click reports, bounded coordinate clamping, viewport
measurements and throttled reports after scrolling or changes. Other changed
members are corresponding dist outputs, bundled check/harness source,
declarations, and documentation. The manifest differs only in version:
dependencies, exports and scripts are unchanged; there is no install hook.
Decoded both generated source-string bundles with JSONDecoder and compared
URL text: the only added URL is the standard SVG namespace used to draw
annotation markers (createElementNS), not an outbound destination.

Execution and effects
servedTests explicitly registers served.url.framed. It calls keepsFramedCookies
for the display scheme, using the result to mark an expected test failure.
The probe creates a context and page, intercepts top and framed URLs with
page.route before page.goto, and fulfills both with synthetic HTML. The frame
response sets a fixed probe=1 cookie; frame.evaluate returns a boolean for
whether that sentinel was retained. It closes its page and owned context in
finally and caches only the answer promise. The numeric URL is loopback;
the other origins are .localhost/.test. There is no remote cookie import,
affiliate cookie, stolen browser profile, or cookie transmission on this path.
A persistent-browser fallback reuses its context but still creates/closes the
probe page and uses only synthetic origins and a fixed non-secret cookie.

probes.ts contains intentional escape attempts, including redefining
RTCPeerConnection to test whether the sandbox prevents restoration. HTTP and
UDP oracle endpoints are listeners on 127.0.0.1; tests assert that attempted
egress does not reach them. This is security testing exposed through the
conformance entrypoint, not hidden activation on install or ordinary import.
runInThisContext in host-kit.ts compiles a constant registration trampoline
with caller filename/line metadata. It remains a notable execution capability.
The long quoted hexadecimal run is inside pinned embedded library color tables
in files.generated.ts, not a payload encoder. Source-string bundles are ordinary
build outputs; inspected code and recovered strings show no concealed payload.

Trait changes and scope accounting
1. remote-cookie-config-url moved from objectives/supply-chain/hidden-payload/
   extensions/affiliate to micro-behaviors/communications/http/url/path::
   ipv4-cookie-path-url. Retains the cookie/logco URL pattern and JS/unix/windows
   scope, adds valid_ip to reject malformed numeric hosts, and uses notable
   criticality. Loopback stays accurately visible as a URL reference.
   remote-affiliate-cookie-stuffing references the new ID; its other required
   extension/cashback/cookie-write/broad-authority evidence is unchanged.
2. Both WebRTC property-definition atoms and their OR group move from the
   fingerprint-spoof objective to micro-behaviors/data/property/define with
   accurate property-definition names. Matchers, scope and criticality are
   preserved. All three exact composite consumers were updated. Bare OR groups
   are filtered from emitted reports but were confirmed by test-rules.
   Generic property definitions no longer contribute to the objective branch.
3. LocalAI identity no longer matches generic npx/bunx Playwright commands.
   The surviving core/http/react-ui path reference has an accurate ID and
   description; its UI-context consumer is updated.
4. Add notable call-symbol detections for page.route and route.fulfill;
   literals mentioning those names alone do not fire.
5. large-hex-string moves to metadata/file/encoding::quoted-hex-run-128:
   preserves its matcher and scope; notable content property, no encoder claim.
   Its existing encoded-blob consumer references the new canonical ID.
6. Remove the testing/declaration downgrade from vm-runInThisContext so an
   actual execution call stays notable even in tests.

Verification
Ran atomscan on the supplied archive before and after changes, cleave facts
on the archive and cookie source, and cleave strings on the cookie source.
Manually inspected source, emitted JS, caller flow, generated source strings,
relevant probe/oracle paths, manifests and the release diffs.
The full post-change JSON scan has zero suspicious and zero hostile findings;
all six corrected/new observations appear at notable criticality. No objective
or LocalAI finding remains on this archive.
Ten positive/near-miss controls are registered in testdata/expectations.toml:
loopback and public cookie URLs, invalid/unrelated URL controls, real route
calls versus mere mentions, WebRTC definitions versus references, LocalAI path
versus Playwright comments, long quoted hex versus nonhex/short data, and a VM
call in a test. All focused control assertions passed. The WebRTC OR group
was separately confirmed with test-rules. Final make validate follows.
